## Approach

I have yet to work with a classification model before, but it seems like simple statistics. In addition, I have not yet encountered a confusion matrix. Below are examples created by gemini with a google search.

```{r}
#| title: sample-confusion-matrix

# Sample data
actual    <- factor(c("Yes", "No", "Yes", "Yes", "No", "Yes", "No", "No"))
predicted <- factor(c("Yes", "No", "No",  "Yes", "No", "Yes", "Yes", "No"))

# Generate simple cross-tabulation
raw_matrix <- table(Predicted = predicted, Actual = actual)
print(raw_matrix)


library(caret)

# Define your data as factors (ensure they have identical levels)
actual    <- factor(c("Yes", "No", "Yes", "Yes", "No", "Yes", "No", "No"), levels = c("Yes", "No"))
predicted <- factor(c("Yes", "No", "No",  "Yes", "No", "Yes", "Yes", "No"), levels = c("Yes", "No"))

# Generate the confusion matrix
# Note: Syntax is confusionMatrix(predictions, references/actuals)
cm <- confusionMatrix(predicted, actual)
print(cm)
```

The caret package might produce the easiest results, but I will have to start working with the data and reviewing the literature before making a decision.
